chunks: The day the Spirit takes its stand, with the angels ranged in rows. None will speak except who is permitted by Ar-Rahman and says what is right.

key_terms.الرَّحْمَٰنُ: Ar-Rahman, the Most Merciful, one of the primary names of God
key_terms.الرُّوحُ: The Spirit, often referring to Jibreel or the soul in eschatological contexts
key_terms.صَفًّا: In rows or lines, indicating order and formation
key_terms.صَوَابًا: Truthfully, correctly, or what is right

ai.seo_question: Who speaks on the Day of Resurrection and under what condition?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the 'Spirit' (Ruh) is often identified as the Archangel Gabriel or the highest angelic entity, emphasizing the hierarchical order of creation on the Day of Judgment. The restriction on speech highlights the absolute sovereignty of Allah, where even the most exalted beings remain silent unless granted specific permission to declare truth, reinforcing the concept of divine authority over all cosmic affairs.
